title: Indian-American Google Executive Sheetal Wrzesien Shot Dead by Husband in Georgia
excerpt: Sheetal Wrzesien, 57, a former senior engineering manager at Google, was killed at her Cobb County home on July 7. Her husband Kirk B. Wrzesien faces five felony charges including murder.
body:
• Sheetal Wrzesien, 57, was found with multiple gunshot wounds at her home in Smyrna, Georgia, and pronounced dead at the scene on July 7
  • Her husband Kirk B. Wrzesien, 56, was arrested and charged with felony murder, two counts of aggravated assault, and two firearms offences
  • The couple's 23-year-old son Jason was also shot and survived after emergency surgery
  • Sheetal was a Georgia Tech alumna with over two decades in technology, including leadership roles at Google and Home Depot

Fatal Shooting at Smyrna Home

Sheetal Wrzesien, a 57-year-old Indian-American technology executive and former senior engineering manager at Google, was shot dead by her husband at the family's residence in Smyrna, Georgia, on the evening of July 7, according to the Cobb County Police Department.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=kw3bvKCQSvs

Officers responded to reports of gunfire at the Wrzesien home on Laurel Creek Trail shortly before 8 p.m. Upon arrival, they found the couple's 23-year-old son, Jason Wrzesien, outside the house suffering from critical gunshot injuries. He was rushed to a local hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery. His current medical condition has not been publicly disclosed.

Inside the residence, police discovered Sheetal Wrzesien with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead at the scene. Law enforcement secured the neighbourhood for several hours as detectives collected evidence and processed the crime scene.

Husband Faces Five Felony Charges

Kirk B. Wrzesien, 56, was arrested at the residence without incident. He has been charged with one count of felony murder, two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon — relating to the attacks on both his wife and son — and two counts of possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony. He is being held without bond at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center.

The Cobb County Police Department said the shooting stemmed from an escalating domestic confrontation within the household. Investigators have not disclosed a specific motive, and the investigation remains ongoing. No additional suspects are being sought.

A Distinguished Career in Technology

Sheetal Wrzesien had built a distinguished career spanning more than two decades in the global technology sector. She earned a Computer Science degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1994 and went on to hold leadership positions at several major companies.

At Google, she served as Engineering and Operations Lead for Data Governance, Content Management, and Customer Relationship Management systems. She later returned to Google as a Marketing Technology Advisor in the Android division, after a brief tenure at the Aspen Institute. At the time of her death, she was serving as Senior Director at GoTo Foods.

Before her time at Google, Wrzesien led large-scale mobile and e-commerce digital transformation projects for major US retail companies, including The Home Depot. She also served on the academic advisory board of Georgia Tech's College of Computing and was widely recognised for mentoring young professionals and encouraging women to pursue careers in STEM fields.

"I've seen him doing yard work. Really nice guy. Very social neighbour. It's a terrible tragedy."

— Peter Lee, Neighbour, to Atlanta News First

Community in Shock

The shooting has sent shockwaves through the predominantly quiet Smyrna neighbourhood. Residents expressed disbelief over the violence in their community. Joanne Anderson, who has lived on Laurel Creek Trail for more than 20 years, told Atlanta News First she was caught off guard by the commotion.

"I didn't know what was going on. I didn't know if someone had a heart attack or what had happened."

— Joanne Anderson, Neighbour, to Atlanta News First

Diaspora Conversations on Domestic Violence

Wrzesien's killing adds to a troubling series of violent incidents involving Indian-Americans in the United States. The case has drawn attention within the Indian diaspora, spotlighting the issue of domestic violence that can remain hidden even in affluent, educated households.

Sheetal Wrzesien spent her early years across England, India, and Ghana before settling in the United States, where she became a respected figure in Atlanta's technology community. Her death has prompted conversations about the need for stronger domestic violence awareness and support networks within the Indian-American community.

Authorities have confirmed that the investigation is focused on a domestic incident within the family. Kirk B. Wrzesien remains in custody awaiting further judicial proceedings.
